overview.text: Mercutio is a witty, quick-tempered friend of Romeo in William Shakespeare’s tragedy Romeo and Juliet, and a relative of Verona’s Prince. His jokes and wordplay provide comic relief, but his readiness to fight also pulls him into the families’ feud. In Act 1, scene 4, he answers Romeo’s anxiety about dreams with the imaginative Queen Mab speech, portraying a tiny fairy whose visits shape people’s dreams. Later, when Tybalt challenges Romeo and Romeo refuses to fight, Mercutio takes up the challenge. Tybalt fatally wounds him as Romeo tries to intervene; his death drives Romeo to kill Tybalt and marks a turning point toward further tragedy.

key_facts.text: Mercutio is a close friend of Romeo and a relative of the Prince of Verona.
In Act 1, scene 4, he describes Queen Mab, a tiny fairy whose visits inspire dreams.
His quick wit and saucy wordplay add comic relief to the play.
After Romeo declines Tybalt’s challenge, Mercutio fights Tybalt and is fatally wounded while Romeo tries to stop them.
His death prompts Romeo to kill Tybalt and helps propel the tragedy that follows.
